qualifying_findings.title: NEAR AI reports SGLang remote-code-execution incident affecting one inference server
topic_areas: public AI security incidents, mitigations, patches, disclosures, and lessons learned
model, dataset, dependency, artifact, runtime, cloud, hardware, and deployment supply chains
qualifying_findings.factual_summary: NEAR AI says an unauthorized party exploited a remote-code-execution vulnerability in SGLang on one inference server, obtained access to internal infrastructure, and could have observed requests processed on that server on November 8, including confidential-mode requests. It reports access to account details for about 100 users, 18 legacy agents, and two API keys exposed in logs; it says stored Private Chat conversations and uploaded files showed no indication of access. NEAR AI revoked sessions and administrative credentials, replaced agent tokens, rotated remaining credentials, deployed the SGLang fix across inference servers, completed a forensic review, and notified confirmed affected users.
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: One NEAR AI inference server running SGLang; legacy NEAR AI Agents deployment; exact SGLang CVE and fixed release not supplied
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: The report is a concrete incident and mitigation record showing that confidential-computing protections do not remove the risk from vulnerable inference software inside the protected environment. It also links inference-runtime compromise to in-flight prompt exposure, legacy-agent data, and credentials in logs.

upstream_routing.classification: upstream-owned entity with downstream-owned security incident lens
upstream_routing.routing_note: Route broad NEAR AI and SGLang ecosystem coverage to ai-wiki. Retain the incident scope, confidential-inference boundary, credential/log exposure, patching, and response lessons in ai-security-wiki.

qualifying_findings.confidence: high for the vendor-stated incident scope and response; the root-cause details and absence-of-access statements remain vendor assertions pending an independent SGLang advisory or forensic report
follow_up_actions: Locate the SGLang project advisory or fix and record its exact version boundary before synthesis.
Keep the distinction between potentially observed in-flight requests and stored Private Chat or uploaded files.
Do not generalize the incident to all confidential-inference deployments.

qualifying_findings.title: CVE-2026-125368 records OmniAgent bash approval-gate bypass through find -execdir
topic_areas: agent and tool security, including MCP, plugins, browsers, delegated authority, and autonomous action
identity, authentication, authorization, credentials, and least privilege
qualifying_findings.evidence_classification: public CVE record corroborated by public project issue and implicated source revision
qualifying_findings.factual_summary: CVE-2026-125368, published and updated November 10, describes an OmniAgent approval bypass through commit 12b98c5. Its safe-bash classifier treats commands beginning with find as safe without separately interpreting find -execdir arguments. The public issue explains that a prompt-injected agent can cause execution of binaries through that primitive without the advertised human-approval step; it remained open at collection time and no fixed release was identified.
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: OmniAgent through commit 12b98c520959eff88a6cfa3dd233497084360ab0, especially ReflexionAgent bash execution with the approval gate enabled; no fixed release stated
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: This is a concrete delegated-authority failure: a shallow safe-command allowlist can turn prompt-influenced tool input into unsupervised execution. The evidence supports parsing or disabling compound-command auto-approval, sandboxing the tool runtime, and independently validating any claimed approval boundary.

upstream_routing.classification: shared concept with downstream-owned security control
upstream_routing.routing_note: Route general OmniAgent and coding-agent workflow coverage to ai-dev-wiki. Retain the approval-gate bypass, prompt-injection precondition, execution-containment, and remediation evidence in ai-security-wiki.

qualifying_findings.confidence: medium-high: the public CVE record, public issue, and pinned source revision agree; the reporter issue is open and a maintainer fix or independently reproduced advisory was not located
follow_up_actions: Check for a maintainer response, release, or advisory before durable synthesis.
Verify whether the current default branch still contains the unsafe classifier before advising a version-specific action.
Treat prompt injection as a stated exploitation precondition rather than a confirmed in-the-wild campaign.
